defects.description: Refresh accepts an unexpired revoked source and issues a usable independent session.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { Sessions } from "./src/index.js"; const s = new Sessions(() => 0); const token = s.issue("alice",10); s.revoke(token); try { const renewed = s.refresh(token,10); const ticket = s.submit(renewed,"hello"); s.dispatch(ticket); } catch {} console.log(JSON.stringify(s.effects()));'

defects.why_missed: S9(a): issue, revoke, refresh, submit, dispatch demonstrates authority resurrection. Testing that the original revoked token is rejected names revocation but is green on every variant; the newly issued credential must actually be exercised.

defects.description: Dispatch checks revocation but omits expiration, allowing an admitted job to execute with an expired session.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { Sessions } from "./src/index.js"; let now = 0; const s = new Sessions(() => now); const token = s.issue("alice",10); const ticket = s.submit(token,"hello"); now = 10; try { s.dispatch(ticket); } catch {} console.log(JSON.stringify(s.effects()));'

defects.why_missed: S9(a,d): issue, submit, clock advance, dispatch requires authorization at execution, not merely admission. An expired-submission rejection test never distinguishes variants; the naive queue oracle expects delivery of an already accepted message.
